section.title: Preface
section.p: This is the Instructors' Guide for the Activities Workbook, which includes a Lesson for each section of the textbook. The Lessons are intended for use in class and present the skills of algebra in the context of modeling and problem-solving. The student version of this PreTeXt document meets accessibility requirements, but there is also a pdf version of the workbook that can be printed out for students, with space for their work, so that they can have a record of the Lesson if they wish. Usually, students should work on the Activities in groups of three or four, while you circulate to answer questions and provide support. For some Lessons it may be more effective to lead the class as a whole in a guided inquiry.

Besides the Activities, the Instructor's Guide includes an introduction and objectives for each Lesson. There are also tips for teaching presented as "asides" near the relevant exercises. At the end of the Lesson there is a section called Checkpoint for students to reflect on their work and how it demonstrates the objectives of the Lesson. Ask students to go over these questions in their groups, then perhaps ask for volumteers to give their answers. The Questions for Writing or Discussion can be used in class, or they could be assigned as writing exercises (especially if you want to include a writing component in your course). They could also appear on quizzes or exams.

We have also provided some activity-specific Concept Questions for each Lesson; if you use "clickers" for these questions, Turning Point will grade them and keep the scores for you. If you make them part of the grade, they can help motivate students to focus on the lesson during class time. Alternatively, the Concept Questions questions can be used as part of a review before exams.

Before coming to class, students should read the assigned section and answer the embedded QuickCheck reading questions. We want students to learn how to read a textbook, rather than relying entirely on an instructor's lecture to provide all the information they need. There is also a Preview set of Homework Problems on the prerequisite skills needed for the section; these can be assigned before class or used as the class opener.

Class time can then be spent primarily on the Activities. You may want to give a brief introduction, but should start on the Activities as soon as possible to allow students sufficient time. Do try to save some time at the end of class for a summary of the Lesson.
